problem: Prior learned ObjectNav work uses discrete actions, simplified physics, or goal vectors, and does not jointly handle object-conditioned exploration, realistic visuals and continuous low-level control. On-policy RL is also sample-inefficient for training such policies at scale.
motivation: Real robots use continuous velocity control in unknown environments where the goal location is unknown, so the agent must explore semantically and avoid collisions. Data is expensive, which favors off-policy RL that can be distributed. The authors want to see what exploration and control behaviors emerge from experience alone.
key_idea: Train an end-to-end ResNet50+LSTM policy with a distributed off-policy Soft Actor-Critic (100 CPU collectors, 8 GPU learners, distributed replay) to output continuous twist commands from RGB, LiDAR and an oracle detection mask in Gibson homes with realistic differential-drive physics.
insight: A simple reward (collision, step, progress, success) is enough for exploration behaviors such as peeking, circling, context use and beelining to emerge. The modality ablation shows that base-mounted LiDAR matters most for collisions (RGB+Depth+Det SR 0.30 vs RGB+LiDAR+Det 0.68 with stuck-on-collision physics). Allowing sliding at collision raises SPL by 0.10-0.20, so realistic collision physics is a major difficulty, and removing the oracle Det mask cuts mean SPL from 0.52 to 0.28.
method: Distributed SAC: 100 CPU collect workers run the policy in the simulator, and 8 GPUs do synchronous SGD with the TF-Agents SAC implementation (98M steps per 24h).
Distributed experience replay buffer: workers send unrolls of up to 100 steps, and the buffer returns uniformly sampled crops of length 20.
Reward: -0.05 on collision, -0.01 per step, 0.1 times geodesic progress toward the goal, and +1.0 on success. There is no exploration supervision.

Observations: RGB (0.88 m height, 79° FOV), depth, 1-D LiDAR (222 points, 220° FOV, base-mounted), previous action, a collision bit, a one-hot goal label, and an optional oracle goal-object binary mask (Det).

Architecture: channel-reduced ResNet50 for the image stack, a 3-layer ConvNet for LiDAR, and MLPs for the auxiliary inputs, each giving a 128-d embedding. The embeddings are summed and fed to a 512-d single-layer LSTM that outputs continuous linear and angular velocity and critic values.

Environment and success criterion: a custom simulator of a LoCoBot/Fetch-like differential-drive robot in Gibson homes with 9 object classes. Success requires a navigable pose within 1 m of the object's 3D box and the object within the central 20% of the RGB view.
Baselines: scripted Roomba and topological-graph traversal, and human raters.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 (channels/4) + LSTM-512 SAC actor-critic (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Online RL experience in 25 training Gibson homes (with 3D semantic annotations); 98M steps per 24h on 8 GPUs
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB + depth + 1-D LiDAR + previous action + collision bit (+ oracle goal-object detection mask in most experiments)
setting.action_space: continuous twist commands (linear and angular velocity) for a differential drive
setting.simulator: Custom Gibson-based simulator with differential-drive physics (LoCoBot)
setting.privileged: Oracle goal-object segmentation mask (Det) in the main results; geodesic distance is used only in the training reward

numbers.eval_set_note: 120 episodes, 10 per each of the 12 test house floors, up to 500 steps, start within 15 m

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not an official leaderboard. Baseline and human numbers are in the paper (Human SPL 0.80/SR 0.86, TGT 0.32/0.50, Roomba 0.30/0.35) but are not listed here.
results: The policy reaches SR 0.68 and SPL 0.58 on unseen Gibson test floors with realistic collision physics, nearly double the SPL of the scripted baselines (TGT 0.32, Roomba 0.30), against human SPL 0.80. LiDAR gives the largest gain among the modalities, and removing the oracle detection mask drops mean SPL to 0.28.
limitations: Relies on an oracle goal detection mask for the main results, and learning recognition end-to-end is much weaker (SPL 0.28).
The LSTM's limited memory leads to revisiting and getting trapped in regions, and the agent still collides in narrow spaces.
Simulation only, with no sim-to-real transfer, and evaluation is small (120 episodes, 9 objects, 12 floors).
